text.p: Police said Thursday a canister with a label indicating it contained sarin, a deadly chemical nerve gas, that was found in the Queens neighbourhood of New York Wednesday, was empty.
"The Department of Defence and the FBI laboratories have determined that the canister did not contain sarin. It was empty," Bob Samuel, a police spokesmen said.

The canister with a hand-printed "sarin" label was discovered Wednesday evening at the home of Lester Deily, 52. He has been charged with reckless endangerment and wilfully possessing noxious materials, he said.
Sarin is the chemical warfare agent used in an attack on the Japanese subway system two years ago in which 12 people were killed and thousands were injured.
Police also found hundreds of gallons of highly flammable liquids and gas, including two other canisters containing compressed air and ether, at the Deily home.
